abstract: Lysosomal Ca2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca2+-imaging-based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca2+ stores, diminished Ca2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca2+ transport, and Tmem184b-deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.
